title: How rogue officers turned a nationwide camera network into a tool for stalking

reports.title: Kechi police lieutenant arrested for using police technology to stalk wife
Former Kechi police lieutenant convicted on stalking charges
A former police officer has been sentenced in Sedgwick County District Court
‘You were spotted’: KS officer who used police cameras to stalk estranged wife sentenced
Wichita moves to tighten access, increase oversight on secretive police surveillance program
How rogue officers turned a nationwide camera network into a tool for stalking

summary:
Kechi Police Lieutenant Victor Heiar was arrested by the Wichita Police Department after investigators found he used his police access to unlawfully search WPD's Flock license plate reader system and track his estranged wife's location. Heiar has been removed from the department and booked into Sedgwick County Jail on one count of stalking and one count of unlawful acts concerning computers. The arrest follows a recent announcement that Wichita and Sedgwick County law enforcement would receive $1.6 million in federal funds for license plate readers and upgraded camera technology.

The article does not state a next court date or further legal steps. Defense attorney Charles O'Hara commented that stalking can be handled as a civil or criminal matter, and that the charge may involve a violated protection order or repeated behavior causing fear. Private investigator Joseph Schillaci called the situation isolated and said public safety is not a concern.
